   \
  "$out" \
| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Check your includes and excludes." 1>&2
  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2

buildGoDir() {
  local cmd="$1" dir="$2"

  declare -a flags
  flags+=(${tags:+-tags=$(concatStringsSep "," tags)})
  flags+=(${ldflags:+-ldflags="${ldflags[*]}"})
  flags+=("-p" "$NIX_BUILD_CORES")
  if (( "${NIX_DEBUG:-0}" >= 1 )); then
    flags+=(-x)
  fi

  if [ "$cmd" = "test" ]; then
    flags+=(-vet=off)
    flags+=($checkFlags)
  fi

  local OUT
  if ! OUT="$(go $cmd "${flags[@]}" $dir 2>&1)"; then
    if ! echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '(no( buildable| non-test)?|build constraints exclude all) Go (source )?files'; then
      echo "$OUT" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT" >&2
  fi
  return 0
}

getGoDirs() {
  local type;
  type="$1"
  if [ -n "$subPackages" ]; then
    echo "$subPackages" | sed "s,\(^\| \),\1./,g"
  else
    find . -type f -name \*$type.go -exec dirname {} \; | grep -v "/vendor/" | sort --unique | grep -v "$exclude"
  fi
}

    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2

   \

| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2

  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$tmpfile" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2

    od -A x -t x1z -v -N 128 "$out" >&2

set -e

   \

| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2

  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$tmpfile" 1>&2
  exit 1

state="/run/nixos/network/addresses/eth1"

echo -n "adding address 2001:db8:1::1/64... "
if out=$(ip addr replace "2001:db8:1::1/64" dev "eth1" nodad 2>&1); then
  echo "done"
else
  echo "'ip addr replace \"2001:db8:1::1/64\" dev \"eth1\"' nodad failed: $out"

fi

  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then

      ln -s "$(readlink -f "$fn")" $out/

 else

    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2

    od -A x -t x1z -v -N 128 "$out" >&2

   \
  "$out" \
| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Check your includes and excludes." 1>&2
  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2

makeCompatibilitySymlink() {
  declare -a outputsToLink=("$out")

  if [ -n "$lib" ]; then
    outputsToLink+=("$lib")

oldOpts="$(shopt -po nounset)" || true
set -euo pipefail

export NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY="$NIX_BUILD_TOP/dummy"
mkdir "$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY"

if test "$staticCompiler" = "1"; then
    EXTRA_LDFLAGS="-static"
elif test "${NIX_DONT_SET_RPATH-}" != "1"; then
    EXTRA_LDFLAGS="-Wl,-rpath,${!outputLib}/lib"
else
    EXTRA_LDFLAGS=""
fi

# GCC interprets empty paths as ".", which we don't want.
if test -z "${CPATH-}"; then unset CPATH; fi
if test -z "${LIBRARY_PATH-}"; then unset LIBRARY_PATH; fi
echo "\$CPATH is \`${CPATH-}'"
echo "\$LIBRARY_PATH is \`${LIBRARY_PATH-}'"

if test "$noSysDirs" = "1"; then

    declare -g \
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD EXTRA_FLAGS EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET \
        EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET

    # Extract flags from Bintools Wrappers
    for post in '_FOR_BUILD' ""; do
        curBintools="NIX_BINTOOLS${post}"

        declare -a extraLDFlags=()
        if [[ -e "${!curBintools}/nix-support/orig-libc" ]]; then
            # Figure out what extra flags when linking to pass to the gcc
            # compilers being generated to make sure that they use our libc.
            extraLDFlags=($(< "${!curBintools}/nix-support/libc-ldflags") $(< "${!curBintools}/nix-support/libc-ldflags-before" || true))
            if [ -e ${!curBintools}/nix-support/ld-set-dynamic-linker ]; then
                extraLDFlags=-dynamic-linker=$(< ${!curBintools}/nix-support/dynamic-linker)
            fi

            # The path to the Libc binaries such as `crti.o'.
            libc_libdir="$(< "${!curBintools}/nix-support/orig-libc")/lib"
        else
            # Hack: support impure environments.
            extraLDFlags=("-L/usr/lib64" "-L/usr/lib")
            libc_libdir="/usr/lib"
        fi
        declare -a prefixExtraLDFlags=()
        prefixExtraLDFlags=("-L$libc_libdir")
        nixDontSetRpathVar=NIX_DONT_SET_RPATH${post}
        if test "${!nixDontSetRpathVar-}" != "1"; then
            prefixExtraLDFlags+=("-rpath" "$libc_libdir")
        fi
        extraLDFlags=("${prefixExtraLDFlags[@]}" "${extraLDFlags[@]}")
        for i in "${extraLDFlags[@]}"; do
            declare -g EXTRA_LDFLAGS${post}+=" -Wl,$i"
        done
    done

    # Extract flags from CC Wrappers
    for post in '_FOR_BUILD' ""; do
        curCC="NIX_CC${post}"
        curFIXINC="NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY${post}"

        declare -a extraFlags=()
        if [[ -e "${!curCC}/nix-support/orig-libc" ]]; then
            # Figure out what extra compiling flags to pass to the gcc compilers
            # being generated to make sure that they use our libc.
            extraFlags=($(< "${!curCC}/nix-support/libc-crt1-cflags") $(< "${!curCC}/nix-support/libc-cflags"))

            # The path to the Libc headers
            libc_devdir="$(< "${!curCC}/nix-support/orig-libc-dev")"

            # Use *real* header files, otherwise a limits.h is generated that
            # does not include Libc's limits.h (notably missing SSIZE_MAX,
            # which breaks the build).
            declare -g NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY${post}="$libc_devdir/include"
        else
            # Hack: support impure environments.
            extraFlags=("-isystem" "/usr/include")
            declare -g NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY${post}=/usr/include
        fi

        extraFlags=("-I${!curFIXINC}" "${extraFlags[@]}")

        # BOOT_CFLAGS defaults to `-g -O2'; since we override it below, make
        # sure to explictly add them so that files compiled with the bootstrap
        # compiler are optimized and (optionally) contain debugging information
        # (info "(gccinstall) Building").
        if test -n "${dontStrip-}"; then
            extraFlags=("-O2" "-g" "${extraFlags[@]}")
        else
            # Don't pass `-g' at all; this saves space while building.
            extraFlags=("-O2" "${extraFlags[@]}")
        fi

        declare -g EXTRA_FLAGS${post}="${extraFlags[*]}"
    done

    if test -z "${targetConfig-}"; then
        # host = target, so the flags are the same
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET="$EXTRA_FLAGS"
        EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET="$EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
    fi

    # We include `-fmacro-prefix-map` in `cc-wrapper` for non‐GCC
    # platforms only, but they get picked up and passed down to
    # e.g. GFortran calls that complain about the option not
    # applying to the language. Hack around it by asking GCC not
    # to complain.
    #
    # TODO: Someone please fix this to do things that make sense.
    if [[ $EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD == *-fmacro-prefix-map* ]]; then
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD+=" -Wno-complain-wrong-lang"
    fi
    if [[ $EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET == *-fmacro-prefix-map* ]]; then
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET+=" -Wno-complain-wrong-lang"
    fi

    # CFLAGS_FOR_TARGET are needed for the libstdc++ configure script to find
    # the startfiles.
    # FLAGS_FOR_TARGET are needed for the target libraries to receive the -Bxxx
    # for the startfiles.
    makeFlagsArray+=(
        "BUILD_SYSTEM_HEADER_DIR=$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY_FOR_BUILD"
        "SYSTEM_HEADER_DIR=$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY_FOR_BUILD"
        "NATIVE_SYSTEM_HEADER_DIR=$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY"

        "LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"
        #"LDFLAGS=$EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
        "LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"

        "CFLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"
        "CXXFLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"
        "FLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"

        # It seems there is a bug in GCC 5
        #"CFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS $EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
        #"CXXFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS $EXTRA_LDFLAGS"

        "CFLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
        "CXXFLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
        "FLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
    )

    if test -z "${targetConfig-}"; then
        makeFlagsArray+=(
            "BOOT_CFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS $EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
            "BOOT_LDFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
        )
    fi

    if test "$withoutTargetLibc" == 1; then
        # We don't want the gcc build to assume there will be a libc providing
        # limits.h in this stage
        makeFlagsArray+=(
            'LIMITS_H_TEST=false'
        )
    else
        makeFlagsArray+=(
            'LIMITS_H_TEST=true'
        )
    fi
fi

makeEtcEntry() {
  src="$1"
  target="$2"
  mode="$3"
  user="$4"
  group="$5"

  if [[ "$src" = *'*'* ]]; then
    # If the source name contains '*', perform globbing.
    mkdir -p "$out/etc/$target"
    for fn in $src; do
        ln -s "$fn" "$out/etc/$target/"
    done
  else

    mkdir -p "$out/etc/$(dirname "$target")"
    if ! [ -e "$out/etc/$target" ]; then
      ln -s "$src" "$out/etc/$target"
    else
      echo "duplicate entry $target -> $src"
      if [ "$(readlink "$out/etc/$target")" != "$src" ]; then
        echo "mismatched duplicate entry $(readlink "$out/etc/$target") <-> $src"
        ret=1
      fi
    fi

    if [ "$mode" != symlink ]; then
      echo "$mode" > "$out/etc/$target.mode"
      echo "$user" > "$out/etc/$target.uid"
      echo "$group" > "$out/etc/$target.gid"
    fi
  fi
}

structuredAttrs.postFetch:
tmpfile="$TMPDIR/patch"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Fetched patch file '$out' is empty!" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

set +e
cat < "$out" > "$tmpfile"
if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2
    echo 'Fetched file was (limited to 128 bytes):' >&2
    od -A x -t x1z -v -N 128 "$out" >&2
    exit 1
fi
set -e
mv "$tmpfile" "$out"

lsdiff \
   \
  "$out" \
| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Check your includes and excludes." 1>&2
  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$tmpfile" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

structuredAttrs.name: gettext-1.0
structuredAttrs.postPatch:
# Older versions of gettext come with a copy of `extern-inline.m4` that is not compatible with clang 18.
# When a project uses gettext + autoreconfPhase, autoreconfPhase will invoke `autopoint -f`, which will
# replace whatever (probably compatible) version of `extern-inline.m4` with one that probalby won’t work
# because `autopoint` will copy the autoconf macros from the project’s required version of gettext.
# Fixing this requires replacing all the older copies of the problematic file with a new one.
#
# This is ugly, but it avoids requiring workarounds in every package using gettext and autoreconfPhase.
declare -a oldFiles=($(tar tf gettext-tools/autotools/archive.dir.tar | grep '^gettext-0\.[19].*/extern-inline.m4'))
oldFilesDir=$(mktemp -d)
for oldFile in "${oldFiles[@]}"; do
  mkdir -p "$oldFilesDir/$(dirname "$oldFile")"
  cp -a gettext-tools/gnulib-m4/extern-inline.m4 "$oldFilesDir/$oldFile"
done
tar uf gettext-tools/autotools/archive.dir.tar --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -C "$oldFilesDir" "${oldFiles[@]}"

substituteAllInPlace gettext-runtime/src/gettext.sh.in
substituteInPlace gettext-tools/projects/KDE/trigger --replace "/bin/pwd" pwd
substituteInPlace gettext-tools/projects/GNOME/trigger --replace "/bin/pwd" pwd
substituteInPlace gettext-tools/src/project-id --replace "/bin/pwd" pwd

def user(command):
    return machine.succeed(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command))

def browser(action, name, **options):
    result = json.loads(user("PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE=/nix/store/2xc3ahwfjaa3k3wpn4gslgws25swsyd7-playwright-core-1.59.1 "
        "CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/nix/store/789yhb4v2kq51jwl4acmmjvxs7mfrlhv-chromium-152.0.7977.75/bin/chromium "
        "/nix/store/l07gdbxylzfl8pbx9pxy6fyg95w4hjwy-nodejs-24.19.0/bin/node /nix/store/77s3vg926n81pdm251wspcrqwbqws1hf-creation_acceptance_browser.cjs "
        + action + " " + name + " " + shlex.quote(json.dumps(options))))
    print(json.dumps(result))
    return result

def checkpoint(name):
    return json.loads(user("cat /tmp/creation-" + name + ".json"))

def status(name):
    request = checkpoint(name)["requestId"]
    return json.loads(user("curl -fsS --unix-socket " + runtime + "/portal.sock "
        + "http://localhost/api/session-creations/" + request))

def restart():
    user("systemctl --user kill --signal=SIGKILL --kill-whom=all workspace-portal@fixture.service")
    user("systemctl --user restart workspace-portal@fixture.service")
    machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "curl -fsS --unix-socket " + runtime
        + "/portal.sock http://localhost/ >/dev/null")

def native(identity):
    return json.loads(user("/nix/store/gf65ylg0vyxygm8j104lxh07vakkswfw-python3-3.13.15-env/bin/python /nix/store/4l8lg9gv02hvnp8naixaw5lbs4hzbmng-creation_transport.py read "
        + runtime + "/app-server.sock " + shlex.quote(identity)))

def naming_proof(name, provider, attempts=1):
    marker = checkpoint(name)["marker"]
    # Keep large request bodies inside the guest. Ignore an incomplete last
    # line from unrelated inference still being logged after naming finished.
    script = ("import json; marker=" + repr(marker) + "; "
        + "rows=[json.loads(line) for line in open('/tmp/creation-model/requests.jsonl') if line.endswith('\\n')]; "
        + "print(json.dumps([row['provider'] for row in rows if row['body'].get('model')=='gpt-6-luna' "
        + "and marker in json.dumps(row['body'].get('input',[]))]))")
    routes = json.loads(user("/nix/store/gf65ylg0vyxygm8j104lxh07vakkswfw-python3-3.13.15-env/bin/python -c " + shlex.quote(script)))
    assert routes == [provider] * attempts, routes

def proof(name, provider, members=0, sensitive=False):
    record = checkpoint(name)
    slug = record["slug"]
    directory = root + "/work/" + slug
    manifest = json.loads(user("/nix/store/gf65ylg0vyxygm8j104lxh07vakkswfw-python3-3.13.15-env/bin/python -c " + shlex.quote(
        "import yaml,json;print(json.dumps(yaml.safe_load(open(" + repr(directory + "/portal.yml") + "))))")))
    assert manifest["codex"]["thread_id"] == record["threadId"], manifest
    assert manifest["creation"]["state"] == "ready", manifest
    if record["kind"] != "fork":
        assert manifest["creation"]["initial_goal_sent"] is True, manifest
    journal_path = root + "/worktrees/.locks/" + slug + ".creation.json"
    if record["kind"] == "fork":
        user("test ! -e " + root + "/worktrees/.locks/" + slug + ".fork.json")
    else:
        journal = json.loads(user("cat " + journal_path))
        assert journal["state"] == "ready", journal
        if record["options"].get("provider"):
            assert journal["provider"] == record["options"]["provider"], journal
    receipt_path = portal_state + "/creations/" + slug + ".json"
    receipt = json.loads(user("cat " + receipt_path))
    assert receipt["receiptId"] == record["receiptId"] and receipt["state"] == "ready", receipt
    evidence_path = portal_state + "/creations/" + slug + "." + record["receiptId"] + ".complete.json"
    evidence = json.loads(user("cat " + evidence_path))
    assert evidence["slug"] == slug and evidence["receiptId"] == record["receiptId"], evidence
    assert evidence["threadId"] == record["threadId"], evidence
    metadata = native(record["threadId"])["thread"]
    assert metadata["modelProvider"] == provider, metadata
    assert metadata["cwd"] == directory, metadata
    assert metadata["model"] == "gpt-5.5" and metadata["reasoningEffort"] == "high", metadata
    assert sum(item.get("type") == "userMessage" and record["marker"] in json.dumps(item)
        for turn in metadata["turns"] for item in turn["items"]) == 1, metadata
    assert len({turn["id"] for turn in metadata["turns"]}) == len(metadata["turns"]), metadata
    roster = json.loads(user("cd " + root + " && " + package + "/bin/dev-session team list " + slug + " --as-is"))
    saved = roster["roster"]
    retained = saved["members"] or []
    assert len(retained) == members, saved
    assert saved["rootThreadId"] == record["threadId"] and saved["slug"] == slug, saved
    assert saved["leadModel"] == "gpt-5.5" and saved["leadEffort"] == "high", saved
    assert saved["leadInstructions"] == "CREATION_LEAD_INSTRUCTIONS: return the fixture reply; do not run tools.", saved
    identities = [record["threadId"]]
    for member in retained:
        assert member["state"] == "ready", member
        assert member["model"] == "gpt-5.5" and member["reasoningEffort"] == "high", member
        assert member["instructions"] == "CREATION_MEMBER_INSTRUCTIONS: inspect only when assigned.", member
        identities.append(member["threadId"])
        member_native = native(member["threadId"])["thread"]
        assert member_native["modelProvider"] == provider, member_native
        assert member_native["cwd"] == directory, member_native
        assert member_native["projectId"] == member["projectId"], member_native
    assert len(set(identities)) == len(identities), identities
    inventory = native("inventory")
    assert not inventory.get("nextCursor"), inventory
    listed = {item["id"] for item in inventory["data"] if item["cwd"] == directory}
    assert record["threadId"] in listed and listed <= set(identities), inventory
    # Native thread/list omits empty previews, including unassigned members
    # with only the durable developer bootstrap. Read the pinned native
    # database without writes to inventory those identities and orphan starts.
    persisted = json.loads(user("/nix/store/gf65ylg0vyxygm8j104lxh07vakkswfw-python3-3.13.15-env/bin/python -c " + shlex.quote(
        "import json,pathlib,sqlite3; "
        "files=list((pathlib.Path.home()/'.codex').glob('state_*.sqlite')); "
        "assert len(files)==1,files; "
        "db=sqlite3.connect(files[0].as_uri()+'?mode=ro',uri=True); "
        "print(json.dumps(db.execute('SELECT id FROM threads WHERE cwd=? AND archived=0',"
        + repr((directory,)) + ").fetchall()))")))
    assert {row[0] for row in persisted} == set(identities), persisted
    if sensitive:
        user("git -C " + root + " check-ignore work/" + slug + "/state.md")
    # The real Go ready proof has already passed; retain independent native
    # identities and durable files so a green browser cannot mask duplicates.
    user("mkdir -p /tmp/creation-evidence/" + name + " && cp " + receipt_path + " " + evidence_path + " "
        + directory + "/portal.yml /tmp/creation-evidence/" + name)
    if record["kind"] != "fork":
        user("cp " + journal_path + " /tmp/creation-evidence/" + name)
    user("printf %s " + shlex.quote(json.dumps(metadata)) + " > /tmp/creation-evidence/" + name + "/native.json")

with subtest("install shipped portal, stock Codex and private external providers"):
    user("mkdir -p ~/.codex " + state + " " + root + "/repos " + root + "/work " + root + "/worktrees ~/origins /tmp/creation-evidence")
    user("printf fixture-private-token > ~/.codex/fixture.token && chmod 0600 ~/.codex/fixture.token")
    # Alternate exists only in the host catalog. Naming must import that
    # definition rather than relying on this global primary configuration.
    config = 'model_provider="primary"\nmodel="gpt-5.5"\nmodel_reasoning_effort="xhigh"\napproval_policy="never"\n[model_providers.primary]\nname="Primary fixture"\nbase_url="http://127.0.0.1:2455/primary/v1"\nwire_api="responses"\nrequires_openai_auth=false\nsupports_websockets=false\n'
    user("printf %s " + shlex.quote(config) + " > ~/.codex/config.toml")
    user("systemd-run --user --unit=creation-model /nix/store/gf65ylg0vyxygm8j104lxh07vakkswfw-python3-3.13.15-env/bin/python /nix/store/036naszzh2dbiifmpdmijy87vpcjvdr8-creation_model.py")
    machine.wait_until_succeeds("curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:2455/primary/v1/models")
    user("git config --global user.name 'Creation fixture' && git config --global user.email fixture@example.invalid")
    user("git config --global url.file:///home/developer/origins/.insteadOf git@github.com:fixture/")
    user("git init --bare --initial-branch=master ~/origins/workspace.git")
    user("git init --initial-branch=master " + root + " && cd " + root
        + " && printf '/worktrees/\\n' > .gitignore && git add .gitignore && git commit -m 'fixture: workspace' "
        + "&& git remote add origin git@github.com:fixture/workspace.git && git push origin master")
    user("nix-env --profile " + state + "/profile --set " + package)
    # Reproduce an old systemctl-created instance alias whose package was
    # collected. Ordinary registration must repair it before creation starts.
    unit_dir = "/home/developer/.config/systemd/user"
    provider_unit = "workspace-codex-provider@fixture.service"
    stale_template = "/nix/store/00000000000000000000000000000000-dev-workspace-0.2.0/share/systemd/user/workspace-codex-provider@.service"
    user("mkdir -p " + unit_dir + "/default.target.wants && ln -s " + stale_template + " " + unit_dir + "/" + provider_unit
        + " && ln -s " + stale_template + " " + unit_dir + "/default.target.wants/" + provider_unit)
    user(package + "/bin/workspace-host register fixture " + root + " --hostname fixture.workspace.example.test")
    assert user("systemctl --user show " + provider_unit + " -p LoadState --value").strip() == "loaded"
    user("systemctl --user is-enabled " + provider_unit)
    user("systemctl --user start " + provider_unit)
    user("systemctl --user is-active " + provider_unit)
    assert user("readlink -f " + unit_dir + "/" + provider_unit).strip() == package + "/share/systemd/user/workspace-codex-provider@.service"
    for service in ["workspace-codex@fixture", "workspace-portal@fixture", "workspace-tmux@fixture", "workspace-router"]:
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "systemctl --user is-active " + service)

try:
    with subtest("custom explicit default provider, solo, notifications, attachment and follow-up"):
        browser("create", "explicit", provider="primary", attachment=True)
        proof("explicit", "primary")
        record = checkpoint("explicit")
        initial = [entry for entry in record["transcript"]["entries"] if record["marker"] in entry.get("text", "")]
        assert any("creation-evidence.txt" in json.dumps(entry) for entry in initial), initial
        initial_native = [item for turn in native(record["threadId"])["thread"]["turns"] for item in turn["items"]
            if item.get("type") == "userMessage" and record["marker"] in json.dumps(item)]
        assert len(initial_native) == 1, initial_native
        text = "\n".join(part["text"] for part in initial_native[0]["content"] if part["type"] == "text")
        attachments = json.loads(text.split("Attached local files (inputs; keep these files outside version control):\n", 1)[1])
        assert len(attachments) == 1 and attachments[0]["name"] == "creation-evidence.txt", attachments
        assert attachments[0]["path"].startswith(portal_state + "/uploads/files/"), attachments
        assert user("cat " + shlex.quote(attachments[0]["path"])) == "CREATION_ATTACHMENT_CONTENT"

    with subtest("automatic naming, inherited default provider, sensitive retained team and notifications off"):
        browser("create", "automatic", auto=True, team="development", sensitive=True, notifications=False)
        proof("automatic", "primary", members=2, sensitive=True)
        naming_proof("automatic", "primary")
        assert checkpoint("automatic")["slug"].endswith("accepted-session")

    with subtest("alternate provider, fork and approved-plan destinations preserve source"):
        browser("create", "alternate", provider="alternate")
        proof("alternate", "alternate")
        browser("fork", "explicit", provider="alternate")
        browser("plan", "explicit", provider="alternate", team="development")
        proof("explicit", "primary")
        proof("explicit-fork", "alternate")
        proof("explicit-plan", "alternate", members=2)
        for kind in ["fork", "plan"]:
            record = checkpoint("explicit-" + kind)
            assert native(record["threadId"])["thread"]["modelProvider"] == "alternate", record

    with subtest("frozen fork settings can be restored while its terminal is subscribed"):
        browser("change-effort", "explicit-fork")
        record = checkpoint("explicit-fork")
        assert native(record["threadId"])["thread"]["reasoningEffort"] == "xhigh"
        slug = record["slug"]
        args = [package + "/bin/workspace-portal", "thread", "ensure-settings", "--require-runtime",
            "--thread-id", record["threadId"], "--socket", runtime + "/app-server.sock",
            "--user-state-root", state, "--workspace", root, "--session-slug", slug,
            "--cwd", root + "/work/" + slug, "--worktrees-dir", root + "/worktrees/" + slug,
            "--portal-base-url", "https://fixture.workspace.example.test",
            "--portal-url", "https://fixture.workspace.example.test/" + slug + "/",
            "--authority-dir", runtime + "/authority", "--tmux-socket", runtime + "/tmux.sock",
            "--codex-command", state + "/codex/current/bin/codex", "--codex-version", "0.163.0",
            "--portal-command", package + "/bin/workspace-portal", "--model", "gpt-5.5", "--effort", "high"]
        wrong = args.copy()
        wrong[wrong.index("--cwd") + 1] += "-foreign"
        machine.fail(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(shlex.join(wrong)))
        assert native(record["threadId"])["thread"]["reasoningEffort"] == "xhigh"
        restored = json.loads(user(shlex.join(args)))
        assert restored == {"model": "gpt-5.5", "reasoningEffort": "high"}, restored
        proof("explicit-fork", "alternate")

    with subtest("failed naming creates usable sessions with distinct fallback names"):
        user("touch /tmp/creation-model/bad-name")
        browser("create", "naming-error", auto=True, provider="alternate", attachment=True)
        proof("naming-error", "alternate")
        naming_proof("naming-error", "alternate")
        first = checkpoint("naming-error")
        assert first["slug"].endswith("-development-session"), first
        initial = [entry for entry in first["transcript"]["entries"] if first["marker"] in entry.get("text", "")]
        assert any("creation-evidence.txt" in json.dumps(entry) for entry in initial), initial
        browser("create", "naming-collision", auto=True)
        proof("naming-collision", "primary")
        naming_proof("naming-collision", "primary")
        second = checkpoint("naming-collision")
        assert second["slug"].startswith(first["slug"] + "-"), second
        assert first["threadId"] != second["threadId"], (first, second)
        user("rm /tmp/creation-model/bad-name")

    # Transport faults forward only real native responses. The application
    # binaries, protocol and ordinary service endpoints remain unchanged.
    socket = runtime + "/app-server.sock"
    user("mv " + socket + " " + socket + ".native")
    user("systemd-run --user --unit=creation-transport /nix/store/gf65ylg0vyxygm8j104lxh07vakkswfw-python3-3.13.15-env/bin/python /nix/store/4l8lg9gv02hvnp8naixaw5lbs4hzbmng-creation_transport.py proxy "
        + socket + " " + socket + ".native")
    machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "test -S " + socket)

    with subtest("reload, interruption and retry before native creation preserve admitted settings"):
        user("touch /tmp/creation-model/hold-root-request")
        browser("admit", "before", provider="alternate", team="development")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds("test -e /tmp/creation-model/root-entered")
        restart()
        user("rm /tmp/creation-model/hold-root-request")
        browser("retry", "before")
        proof("before", "alternate", members=2)

    with subtest("lost accepted initial-send reply and portal restart do not repeat the user turn"):
        user("rm -f /tmp/creation-model/send-accepted")
        user("touch /tmp/creation-model/hold-send-reply /tmp/creation-model/hold-turn")
        browser("admit", "after", provider="alternate", team="development")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds("test -e /tmp/creation-model/send-accepted")
        accepted = json.loads(user("cat /tmp/creation-model/send-accepted"))
        accepted_native = native(accepted["threadId"])["thread"]
        assert accepted_native["cwd"] == root + "/work/" + status("after")["slug"], accepted_native
        assert any(turn["id"] == accepted["turnId"] and any(item.get("type") == "userMessage" and
            "CREATION_INITIAL_after" in json.dumps(item) for item in turn["items"])
            for turn in accepted_native["turns"]), accepted_native
        restart()
        user("rm /tmp/creation-model/hold-send-reply /tmp/creation-model/hold-turn")
        browser("retry", "after")
        proof("after", "alternate", members=2)
        user("systemctl --user stop creation-transport && rm -f " + socket + " && mv " + socket + ".native " + socket)

    with subtest("ordinary deletion fences the stale creation request"):
        record = checkpoint("alternate")
        browser("delete-stale", "alternate")
        user("test ! -e " + root + "/work/" + record["slug"])
except Exception:
    print(user("journalctl --user --no-pager -n 180 -u workspace-portal@fixture -u workspace-codex@fixture -u creation-transport"))
    print(user("find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name 'creation-*.json' -exec cat {} \\;"))
    raise
finally:
    machine.copy_from_vm("/tmp/creation-evidence", "creation-evidence")
    machine.copy_from_vm("/tmp/creation-model", "creation-model")

# Get the path to the config util
cfg=$(basename $dev/bin/ncurses*-config)

# symlink the full suffixed include directory

# replace whatever (probably compatible) version of `extern-inline.m4` with one that probalby won’t work

oldFilesDir=$(mktemp -d)
for oldFile in "${oldFiles[@]}"; do
  mkdir -p "$oldFilesDir/$(dirname "$oldFile")"
  cp -a gettext-tools/gnulib-m4/extern-inline.m4 "$oldFilesDir/$oldFile"
done
tar uf gettext-tools/autotools/archive.dir.tar --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -C "$oldFilesDir" "${oldFiles[@]}"

    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2
    echo 'Fetched file was (limited to 128 bytes):' >&2

  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2

env.text:
import json
import shlex
import time

machine.start(allow_reboot=True)
machine.wait_for_unit("user@1000.service")
package = "/nix/store/60a92ypy1s9x36vhprqff39r7pycaz5i-dev-workspace-0.2.0"
user_prefix = "runuser -u developer -- env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 "

def user(command):
    return machine.succeed(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command))

def assert_services():
    machine.wait_for_unit("user@1000.service")
    for unit in ["workspace-tmux@fixture", "workspace-codex@fixture",
                 "workspace-portal@fixture", "workspace-router"]:
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "systemctl --user is-active " + unit)
        assert user("systemctl --user is-enabled " + unit).strip() == "enabled"
    after = user("systemctl --user show workspace-portal@fixture -p After --value")
    assert "workspace-tmux@fixture.service" in after
    assert "workspace-codex@fixture.service" in after
    for socket in ["app-server.sock", "tmux.sock"]:
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "test -S "
                                   "/run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/" + socket)

with subtest("install private user profile and enable real application units"):
    user("mkdir -p ~/.local/state/dev-workspaces ~/workspace/repos "
         "~/workspace/work ~/workspace/worktrees")
    user("umask 077; printf synthetic-only > ~/provider.token")
    user("nix-env --profile ~/.local/state/dev-workspaces/profile --set " + package)
    user("git -C ~/workspace init --initial-branch=master")
    user(package + "/bin/workspace-host register fixture /home/developer/workspace "
         "--hostname fixture.workspace.example.test")
    assert_services()

state_path = "/home/developer/.local/state/dev-workspaces/providers/fixture/state.json"
host = package + "/bin/workspace-host"
worker = "workspace-codex-provider@fixture.service"
codex_unit = "workspace-codex@fixture.service"

diagnostic_start = machine.succeed("date +%s").strip()
assert diagnostic_start.isdigit()

def collect_provider_diagnostics():
    commands = [
        "journalctl --user --no-pager --output=short-monotonic --since=@" + diagnostic_start
        + " --unit=" + worker + " --unit=" + codex_unit
        + " --unit=workspace-codex-reconcile.service --unit=workspace-coordination-gc.service | tail -c 65536",
        "systemctl --user show " + worker + " " + codex_unit
        + " workspace-codex-reconcile.service workspace-coordination-gc.service"
        + " --property=ActiveState,SubState,MainPID,Result,ExecMainStatus,NRestarts",
        "/nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 /nix/store/dpks97v67zlaq0fw56554rnx8hjb35rx-recovery-fixture-metadata.py",
    ]
    for command in commands:
        try:
            status, output = machine.execute(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command), timeout=10)
            print(output)
            print("PROVIDER_DIAGNOSTIC_COLLECTION_STATUS=" + str(status))
        except Exception:
            print("PROVIDER_DIAGNOSTIC_COLLECTION_UNAVAILABLE")

def wait_provider_result(predicate):
    # A terminal result returns to Python. A nonzero shell exit alone would
    # keep wait_until_succeeds polling an already-failed operation for 900s.
    command = "/nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(
        "import json; d=json.load(open(" + repr(state_path) + ")); o=d['operation']; "
        "expected=(" + predicate + "); terminal=o['phase'] in ['applied','failed','canceled']; "
        "assert expected or terminal; "
        "print('PROVIDER_EXPECTED_RESULT' if expected else 'PROVIDER_UNEXPECTED_TERMINAL')")
    try:
        output = machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command))
        assert "PROVIDER_UNEXPECTED_TERMINAL" not in output, "provider reached an unexpected terminal phase"
        return json.loads(user(host + " provider status fixture"))
    except Exception:
        collect_provider_diagnostics()
        raise

def wait_phase(phase):
    return wait_provider_result("o['phase'] == " + repr(phase))

def legacy_provider_request(target, identity):
    # Only retained schema-1 requests use the daemon-restart engine. New
    # public requests intentionally select scoped-v1, even in an empty workspace.
    user("systemctl --user stop " + worker)
    catalog = json.loads(user(package + "/bin/workspace-portal codex-provider catalog "
                              "--catalog /etc/dev-workspaces/codex-providers.json"))
    seed = (
        "import datetime,json,os; p=" + repr(state_path) + "; "
        "os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),mode=0o700,exist_ok=True); "
        "d=json.load(open(p)) if os.path.exists(p) else "
        + repr({"schema": 1, "workspace": "fixture", "root": "/home/developer/workspace",
                "socket": "/run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/app-server.sock", "active": "openai"})
        + "; assert d['schema']==1; "
        "now=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(); "
        "d['operation']=" + repr({"id": identity, "target": target,
                                  "catalogDigest": catalog["digest"], "phase": "waiting", "blockers": []})
        + "; d['operation'].update(createdAt=now,updatedAt=now); "
        "os.umask(0o077); open(p,'w').write(json.dumps(d))"
    )
    user("/nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(seed))
    user("systemctl --user enable --now " + worker)

with subtest("retained legacy requests wait for foreign cgroup processes"):
    foreign_pid = machine.succeed("/nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(
        "import subprocess; p=subprocess.Popen(['sleep','300'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,start_new_session=True); print(p.pid)")).strip()

    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2

  "$out" \
| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2

env.buildCommand:

# Set a reasonable $PATH for programs called by udev rules.

for i in $packages; do
  echo "Adding rules for package $i"
  for j in $i/{etc,lib}/udev/rules.d/*; do
    echo "Copying $j to $out/$(basename $j)"
    cat $j > $out/$(basename $j)
  done
done

# Fix some paths in the standard udev rules.  Hacky.
for i in $out/*.rules; do
  substituteInPlace $i \
    --replace-quiet \"/sbin/modprobe \"/nix/store/ahni4ky7vcyga5rkfk6yil6g0293qyvk-kmod-31/bin/modprobe \
    --replace-quiet \"/sbin/mdadm \"/nix/store/i3p2mqi7xc77inxsw127njlpcz0cj234-mdadm-4.4/sbin/mdadm \
    --replace-quiet \"/sbin/blkid \"/nix/store/4n075ll5jdwbjv142yg8ymz5f3yf4pam-util-linux-2.42.2-bin/sbin/blkid \
    --replace-quiet \"/bin/mount \"/nix/store/4n075ll5jdwbjv142yg8ymz5f3yf4pam-util-linux-2.42.2-bin/bin/mount \
    --replace-quiet /usr/bin/readlink /nix/store/gph17gb73p6qbrqqjnypfjj5npf0ldyx-coreutils-9.11/bin/readlink \
    --replace-quiet /usr/bin/cat /nix/store/gph17gb73p6qbrqqjnypfjj5npf0ldyx-coreutils-9.11/bin/cat \
    --replace-quiet /usr/bin/basename /nix/store/gph17gb73p6qbrqqjnypfjj5npf0ldyx-coreutils-9.11/bin/basename 2>/dev/null

done

echo -n "Checking that all programs called by relative paths in udev rules exist in /nix/store/0xiinbh7pbj479i5v28mqnjrvhvbdibf-systemd-260.2/lib/udev... "
import_progs=$(grep 'IMPORT{program}="[^/$]' $out/* |
  sed -e 's/.*IMPORT{program}="\([^ "]*\)[ "].*/\1/' | uniq)
run_progs=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' $out/* | grep 'RUN+="[^/$]' |
  sed -e 's/.*RUN+="\([^ "]*\)[ "].*/\1/' | uniq)
for i in $import_progs $run_progs; do
  if [[ ! -x /nix/store/0xiinbh7pbj479i5v28mqnjrvhvbdibf-systemd-260.2/lib/udev/$i && ! $i =~ socket:.* ]]; then
    echo "FAIL"
    echo "$i is called in udev rules but not installed by udev"
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "OK"

echo -n "Checking that all programs called by absolute paths in udev rules exist... "
import_progs=$(grep 'IMPORT{program}="/' $out/* |
  sed -e 's/.*IMPORT{program}="\([^ "]*\)[ "].*/\1/' | uniq)
run_progs=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' $out/* | grep 'RUN+="/' |
  sed -e 's/.*RUN+="\([^ "]*\)[ "].*/\1/' | uniq)
for i in $import_progs $run_progs; do
  # if the path refers to /run/current-system/systemd, replace with config.systemd.package
  if [[ $i == /run/current-system/systemd* ]]; then
    i="/nix/store/0xiinbh7pbj479i5v28mqnjrvhvbdibf-systemd-260.2/${i#/run/current-system/systemd/}"
  fi

  if [[ ! -x $i ]]; then
    echo "FAIL"
    echo "$i is called in udev rules but is not executable or does not exist"
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "OK"

filesToFixup="$(for i in "$out"/*; do
  # list all files referring to (/usr)/bin paths, but allow references to /bin/sh.
  grep -P -l '\B(?!\/bin\/sh\b)(\/usr)?\/bin(?:\/.*)?' "$i" || :
done)"

if [ -n "$filesToFixup" ]; then
  echo "Consider fixing the following udev rules:"
  echo "$filesToFixup" | while read localFile; do
    remoteFile="origin unknown"
    for i in /nix/store/xqnpbmfzsxxlxfyf1kqwvk2bnnwxkp73-ipv6-privacy-extensions.rules /nix/store/0kkby9818c90nkahlcjkrrqzdrj0h9ik-ipv6-privacy-extensions.rules /nix/store/gnx0alh2mrc2ndjs7ik6jm3w7avld56w-lvm2-2.03.39 /nix/store/xp99bvc5brkxdl13y1i99ih4ia9w6q7h-bcache-tools-1.1 /nix/store/1m4cq2cffnqzwvg9vkdk1f9bq26qv7px-extra-udev-rules /nix/store/zl3wfq23cjhqwdggqfn173qr20xp1zlx-extra-hwdb-file; do
      for j in "$i"/*/udev/rules.d/*; do
        [ -e "$out/$(basename "$j")" ] || continue
        [ "$(basename "$j")" = "$(basename "$localFile")" ] || continue
        remoteFile="originally from $j"
        break 2
      done
    done
    refs="$(
      grep -o '\B\(/usr\)\?/s\?bin/[^ "]\+' "$localFile" \
        | sed -e ':r;N;${s/\n/ and /;br};s/\n/, /g;br'
    )"
    echo "$localFile ($remoteFile) contains references to $refs."
  done
  exit 1
fi

# https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/e488e300f5c01289c10906c2e53a8e43d6de32d8/configure.ac#L78
sysconfigdataName="$(make --eval $'print-sysconfigdata-name:
\t@echo _sysconfigdata_$(ABIFLAGS)_$(MACHDEP)_$(MULTIARCH) ' print-sysconfigdata-name)"

# The CPython interpreter contains a _sysconfigdata_<platform specific suffix>
# module that is imported by the sysconfig and distutils.sysconfig modules.
# The sysconfigdata module is generated at build time and contains settings
# required for building Python extension modules, such as include paths and
# other compiler flags. By default, the sysconfigdata module is loaded from
# the currently running interpreter (ie. the build platform interpreter), but
# when cross-compiling we want to load it from the host platform interpreter.
# This can be done using the _PYTHON_SYSCONFIGDATA_NAME environment variable.
# The _PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM variable also needs to be set to get the correct
# platform suffix on extension modules. The correct values for these variables
# are not documented, and must be derived from the configure script (see links
# below).
cat <<EOF >> "$out/nix-support/setup-hook"
sysconfigdataHook() {
  if [ "\$1" = '$out' ]; then
    export _PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM='linux-x86_64'
    export _PYTHON_SYSCONFIGDATA_NAME='$sysconfigdataName'
  fi
}

addEnvHooks "\$hostOffset" sysconfigdataHook
EOF
structuredAttrs.postInstall:
# needed for some packages, especially packages that backport functionality
# to 2.x from 3.x
for item in $out/lib/python3.14/test/*; do
  if [[ "$item" != */test_support.py*
     && "$item" != */test/support
     && "$item" != */test/libregrtest
     && "$item" != */test/regrtest.py* ]]; then
    rm -rf "$item"
  else
    echo $item
  fi
done
touch $out/lib/python3.14/test/__init__.py

# Determinism: Windows installers were not deterministic.
# We're also not interested in building Windows installers.
find "$out" -name 'wininst*.exe' | xargs -r rm -f

# Use Python3 as default python
ln -s "$out/bin/idle3" "$out/bin/idle"
ln -s "$out/bin/pydoc3" "$out/bin/pydoc"
ln -s "$out/bin/python3" "$out/bin/python"
ln -s "$out/bin/python3-config" "$out/bin/python-config"
ln -s "$out/lib/pkgconfig/python3.pc" "$out/lib/pkgconfig/python.pc"
ln -sL "$out/share/man/man1/python3.1.gz" "$out/share/man/man1/python.1.gz"

# Get rid of retained dependencies on -dev packages, and remove
# some $TMPDIR references to improve binary reproducibility.
# Note that the .pyc file of _sysconfigdata.py should be regenerated!
for i in $out/lib/python3.14/_sysconfigdata*.py $out/lib/python3.14/config-3.14*/Makefile; do
   sed -i $i -e "s|$TMPDIR|/no-such-path|g"
done

# Further get rid of references. https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/51668
find $out/lib/python*/config-* -type f -print -exec nuke-refs -e /1rz4g4znpzjwh1xymhjpm42vipw92pr73vdgl6xs1hycac8kf2n9 -e /nix/store/n8fqcpnr5ni28l3i9svqa70wz46798v9-tzdata-2026d '{}' +
find $out/lib -name '_sysconfigdata*.py*' -print -exec nuke-refs -e /1rz4g4znpzjwh1xymhjpm42vipw92pr73vdgl6xs1hycac8kf2n9 -e /nix/store/n8fqcpnr5ni28l3i9svqa70wz46798v9-tzdata-2026d '{}' +

# Make the sysconfigdata module accessible on PYTHONPATH
# This allows build Python to import host Python's sysconfigdata
mkdir -p "$out/lib/python3.14/site-packages"
ln -s "$out/lib/python3.14/"_sysconfigdata*.py "$out/lib/python3.14/site-packages/"
# Get rid of retained dependencies on -dev packages, and remove from _sysconfig_vars*.json introduced with Python3.14
for i in $out/lib/python3.14/_sysconfig_vars*.json; do
   sed -i $i -e "s|$TMPDIR|/no-such-path|g"
done
find $out/lib -name '_sysconfig_vars*.json*' -print -exec nuke-refs -e /1rz4g4znpzjwh1xymhjpm42vipw92pr73vdgl6xs1hycac8kf2n9 -e /nix/store/n8fqcpnr5ni28l3i9svqa70wz46798v9-tzdata-2026d '{}' +
ln -s "$out/lib/python3.14/"_sysconfig_vars*.json "$out/lib/python3.14/site-packages/"
# Include a sitecustomize.py file
cp /nix/store/gx4pa1m75g8rrrggj7gi3bg38m4lg3q5-sitecustomize.py $out/lib/python3.14/site-packages/sitecustomize.py
# Determinism: deterministic bytecode
# First we delete all old bytecode.
find $out -type d -name __pycache__ -print0 | xargs -0 -I {} rm -rf "{}"
# Python 3.7 implements PEP 552, introducing support for deterministic bytecode.
# compileall uses the therein introduced checked-hash method by default when
# `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set.
# We exclude lib2to3 because that's Python 2 code which fails
# We build 3 levels of optimized bytecode. Note the default level, without optimizations,
# is not reproducible yet. https://bugs.python.org/issue29708
# Not creating bytecode will result in a large performance loss however, so we do build it.
find $out -name "*.py" | $out/bin/python -m compileall -q -f -x "lib2to3" -i -
find $out -name "*.py" | $out/bin/python -O  -m compileall -q -f -x "lib2to3" -i -
find $out -name "*.py" | $out/bin/python -OO -m compileall -q -f -x "lib2to3" -i -
# *strip* shebang from libpython gdb script - it should be dual-syntax and
# interpretable by whatever python the gdb in question is using, which may
# not even match the major version of this python. doing this after the
# bytecode compilations for the same reason - we don't want bytecode generated.
mkdir -p $out/share/gdb
sed '/^#!/d' Tools/gdb/libpython.py > $out/share/gdb/libpython.py

# Disable system-wide pip installation. See https://peps.python.org/pep-0668/.
cat <<'EXTERNALLY_MANAGED' > $out/lib/python3.14/EXTERNALLY-MANAGED
[externally-managed]
Error=This command has been disabled as it tries to modify the immutable
 `/nix/store` filesystem.

 To use Python with Nix and nixpkgs, have a look at the online documentation:
 <https://nixos.org/manual/nixpkgs/stable/#python>.
EXTERNALLY_MANAGED

# Attempt to purify some of the host info collection
sed -E -i -e 's/uname -r/echo/g' -e 's/uname -n/echo nixpkgs/g' config.guess
sed -E -i -e 's/uname -r/echo/g' -e 's/uname -n/echo nixpkgs/g' configure
# Also override the auto-detection in `configure`.

export CFLAGS_NODIST="-fno-semantic-interposition"

structuredAttrs.name: pytest9-compat-2.patch
structuredAttrs.postFetch:
tmpfile="$TMPDIR/patch"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Fetched patch file '$out' is empty!" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

set +e
cat < "$out" > "$tmpfile"
if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2
    echo 'Fetched file was (limited to 128 bytes):' >&2
    od -A x -t x1z -v -N 128 "$out" >&2
    exit 1
fi
set -e
mv "$tmpfile" "$out"

lsdiff \
   \
  "$out" \
| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Check your includes and excludes." 1>&2
  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$tmpfile" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

sed '2i echo Skipping du threshold test && exit 77' -i ./tests/du/threshold.sh
sed '2i echo Skipping cp reflink-auto test && exit 77' -i ./tests/cp/reflink-auto.sh

sed '2i echo Skipping env test && exit 77' -i ./tests/env/env.sh

sed '2i echo Skipping du long-from-unreadable test && exit 77' -i ./tests/du/long-from-unreadable.sh

# The test tends to fail on cephfs
sed '2i echo Skipping df total-verify test && exit 77' -i ./tests/df/total-verify.sh

# Some target platforms, especially when building inside a container have
# issues with the inotify test.
sed '2i echo Skipping tail inotify dir recreate test && exit 77' -i ./tests/tail/inotify-dir-recreate.sh

# sandbox does not allow setgid
sed '2i echo Skipping chmod setgid test && exit 77' -i ./tests/chmod/setgid.sh
substituteInPlace ./tests/install/install-C.sh \
  --replace 'mode3=2755' 'mode3=1755'

# Fails on systems with a rootfs. Looks like a bug in the test, see
# https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-coreutils/2019-12/msg00000.html
sed '2i print "Skipping df skip-rootfs test"; exit 77' -i ./tests/df/skip-rootfs.sh

# these tests fail in the unprivileged nix sandbox (without nix-daemon) as we break posix assumptions
for f in ./tests/chgrp/{basic.sh,recurse.sh,default-no-deref.sh,no-x.sh,posix-H.sh}; do
  sed '2i echo Skipping chgrp && exit 77' -i "$f"
done
for f in gnulib-tests/{test-chown.c,test-fchownat.c,test-lchown.c}; do
  echo "int main() { return 77; }" > "$f"
done

# We don't have localtime in the sandbox
for f in gnulib-tests/{test-localtime_r.c,test-localtime_r-mt.c}; do
  echo "int main() { return 77; }" > "$f"
done

# These tests sometimes fail on ZFS-backed NFS filesystems
sed '2i echo "Skipping test: fails on zfs " && exit 77' -i gnulib-tests/test-file-has-acl-1.sh
sed '2i echo "Skipping test: fails on zfs " && exit 77' -i gnulib-tests/test-set-mode-acl-1.sh
sed '2i echo "Skipping test: ls/removed-directory" && exit 77' -i ./tests/ls/removed-directory.sh

# intermittent failures on builders, unknown reason
sed '2i echo Skipping du basic test && exit 77' -i ./tests/du/basic.sh

# flaky on some filesystems due to non-deterministic disk usage
sed '2i echo Skipping du deref test && exit 77' -i ./tests/du/deref.sh
sed '2i echo Skipping du inacc-dir test && exit 77' -i ./tests/du/inacc-dir.sh

# fails when syscalls related to acl not being available, e.g. in sandboxed environment
sed '2i echo Skipping ls -al with acl test && exit 77' -i ./tests/ls/acl.sh

env.name: unit-script-linger-users-start
env.text:
#!/nix/store/rzl7zd3zx56vl7m55x1l49sr4xx2bb7y-bash-5.3p9/bin/bash
set -e

declare -a lingeringUserNames=()
declare -a nonLingeringUserNames=()

user_configured () {
    # Use `id` to check if the user exists rather than checking the
    # NixOS configuration, as it may be that the user has been
    # manually configured, which is permitted if users.mutableUsers
    # is true (the default).
    id "$1" >/dev/null
}

shopt -s dotglob nullglob
for user in *; do
    if ! user_configured "$user"; then
        # systemd has this user configured to linger despite them not
        # existing.
        echo "Removing linger for missing user $user" >&2
        rm -- "$user"
    fi
done

if (( ${#nonLingeringUserNames[*]} > 0 )); then
    /nix/store/0xiinbh7pbj479i5v28mqnjrvhvbdibf-systemd-260.2/bin/loginctl disable-linger "${nonLingeringUserNames[@]}"
fi
if (( ${#lingeringUserNames[*]} > 0 )); then
    /nix/store/0xiinbh7pbj479i5v28mqnjrvhvbdibf-systemd-260.2/bin/loginctl enable-linger "${lingeringUserNames[@]}"
fi

env.testScript:
import json
import shlex

machine.start()
machine.wait_for_unit("user@1000.service")
package = "/nix/store/60a92ypy1s9x36vhprqff39r7pycaz5i-dev-workspace-0.2.0"
root = "/home/developer/workspace"
state = "/home/developer/.local/state/dev-workspaces"
user_prefix = "runuser -u developer -- env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 "
cli = package + "/bin/dev-session"

def user(command):
    return machine.succeed(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command))

def browser(slug, action):
    output = user("PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE=/nix/store/2xc3ahwfjaa3k3wpn4gslgws25swsyd7-playwright-core-1.59.1 "
                  "CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/nix/store/789yhb4v2kq51jwl4acmmjvxs7mfrlhv-chromium-152.0.7977.75/bin/chromium "
                  "/nix/store/l07gdbxylzfl8pbx9pxy6fyg95w4hjwy-nodejs-24.19.0/bin/node /nix/store/b2grg67qrpxsvjr1d2f6klrrfbd6c56m-archive_lifecycle_browser.cjs "
                  + shlex.quote(slug) + " " + action)
    return json.loads(output)

def operation(slug):
    output = user("curl -fsS --unix-socket /run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/portal.sock "
                  + "http://localhost/api/sessions/" + slug + "/operation")
    return json.loads(output)

def wait_operation(slug, wanted):
    # Fail on an unexpected terminal result instead of polling it until timeout.
    command = "curl -fsS --unix-socket /run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/portal.sock "
    command += "http://localhost/api/sessions/" + slug + "/operation"
    command += " | /nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(
        "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); "
        "assert d.get('state') in ['complete','failed','paused']; print(json.dumps(d))")
    output = machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command))
    result = json.loads(output)
    assert result["state"] == wanted, result
    return result

def unit(receipt):
    return "workspace-archive-" + receipt["receiptId"] + "-" + str(receipt["attempt"]) + ".service"

def fixture(slug):
    user("cd " + root + " && " + cli + " start " + slug + " --as-is --no-codex --no-attach")
    user("cd " + root + " && " + cli + " worktree add " + slug + " project --as-is")
    checkout = root + "/worktrees/" + slug + "/project"
    user("cd " + checkout + " && printf staged > tracked.txt && git add tracked.txt "
         "&& printf unstaged > tracked.txt && printf untracked > untracked.txt "
         "&& printf ignored > ignored.tmp")
    # Commit substantive tracking so ordinary CLI creation/revival proofs apply.
    user("cd " + root + " && git add work/" + slug + " && git commit -m 'fixture: session' "
         "&& git push origin master")
    return checkout

def assert_restored(slug, checkout):
    assert user("cat " + checkout + "/tracked.txt") == "unstaged"
    assert user("git -C " + checkout + " show :tracked.txt") == "staged"
    assert user("cat " + checkout + "/untracked.txt") == "untracked"
    assert user("cat " + checkout + "/ignored.tmp") == "ignored"
    assert user("git -C " + checkout + " symbolic-ref --short HEAD").strip() == slug

def archived(slug, checkout):
    result = wait_operation(slug, "complete")
    # Operation GET is cache-only; target publication follows its own cadence.
    # Keep terminal failures strict, then wait for this receipt's target view.
    command = "curl -fsS --unix-socket /run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/portal.sock "
    command += "http://localhost/api/sessions/" + slug + "/operation"
    command += " | /nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(
        "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); "
        "assert d.get('receiptId') == " + repr(result["receiptId"]) + " and "
        "d.get('state') == 'complete' and d.get('currentTarget', {}).get('archived') is True, d; "
        "print(json.dumps(d))")
    result = json.loads(machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command), timeout=60))
    user("test ! -e " + checkout + " && test -d " + root + "/archive/" + slug)
    user("git --git-dir=" + root + "/repos/project.git rev-parse refs/heads/" + slug)
    return result

def revive(slug, checkout):
    browser(slug, "revive")
    wait_operation(slug, "complete")
    assert_restored(slug, checkout)

def diagnostics():
    print(user("journalctl --user --no-pager -n 100 -u 'workspace-archive-*' -u workspace-portal@fixture"))
    print(user("find " + root + "/worktrees/.locks -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.archive*.json' -exec cat {} \\;"))

with subtest("install real package and user services with private Git origins"):
    user("mkdir -p " + state + " " + root + "/repos " + root + "/work " + root + "/worktrees")
    user("git config --global user.name 'Archive fixture' && git config --global user.email fixture@example.invalid")
    user("git config --global url.file:///home/developer/origins/.insteadOf git@github.com:fixture/")
    user("mkdir ~/origins && git init --bare --initial-branch=master ~/origins/workspace.git "
         "&& git init --bare --initial-branch=master ~/origins/project.git")
    user("git init --initial-branch=master ~/seed && cd ~/seed && printf base > tracked.txt "
         "&& printf '*.tmp\\n' > .gitignore && git add . && git commit -m 'fixture: base' "
         "&& git remote add origin git@github.com:fixture/project.git && git push origin master")
    user("git init --initial-branch=master " + root + " && cd " + root + " "
         "&& printf '/repos/\\n/worktrees/\\n' > .gitignore && git add .gitignore "
         "&& git commit -m 'fixture: workspace' && git remote add origin git@github.com:fixture/workspace.git "
         "&& git push origin master && git clone --bare git@github.com:fixture/project.git repos/project.git")
    user("git --git-dir=" + root + "/repos/project.git config remote.origin.fetch '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' "
         "&& git --git-dir=" + root + "/repos/project.git fetch origin "
         "&& git --git-dir=" + root + "/repos/project.git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD refs/remotes/origin/master")
    user("nix-env --profile " + state + "/profile --set " + package)
    user(package + "/bin/workspace-host register fixture " + root + " --hostname fixture.workspace.example.test")
    for service in ["workspace-codex@fixture", "workspace-portal@fixture", "workspace-tmux@fixture", "workspace-router"]:
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "systemctl --user is-active " + service)
    # Disable automatic retries only inside this disposable VM; tests drive sync explicitly.
    user("systemctl --user stop workspace-tracking-sync@fixture.timer")

try:
    with subtest("browser archive and revive preserve dirty files and index"):
        slug = "2026-10-17-roundtrip"
        checkout = fixture(slug)
        accepted = browser(slug, "archive")
        completed = archived(slug, checkout)
        assert accepted["receiptId"] == completed["receiptId"]
        assert user("systemctl --user show " + unit(completed) + " -p ExecMainStatus --value").strip() == "0"
        revive(slug, checkout)

    with subtest("accepted archive waits for shared session access across portal restart"):
        slug = "2026-10-19-contended-archive"
        checkout = fixture(slug)
        lock = "/run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/authority/" + slug + ".lock"
        holder = "archive-lock-holder.service"
        user("systemd-run --user --quiet --unit=" + holder + " /nix/store/4n075ll5jdwbjv142yg8ymz5f3yf4pam-util-linux-2.42.2-bin/bin/flock -s "
             + lock + " /nix/store/pkf547jp8a92k4wmxikkyby58w10pysr-bash-interactive-5.3p9/bin/bash -c 'touch /tmp/archive-lock-ready; exec sleep infinity'")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "test -f /tmp/archive-lock-ready")
        accepted = browser(slug, "archive")
        command = "curl -fsS --unix-socket /run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/portal.sock "
        command += "http://localhost/api/sessions/" + slug + "/operation"
        command += " | /nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(
            "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d.get('state') == 'running' and "
            "d.get('progress', {}).get('stage') == 'Waiting for session access', d")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command), timeout=60)
        user("test -d " + checkout + " && test ! -f " + root + "/worktrees/.locks/" + slug + ".archive.json")
        worker = unit(accepted)
        before = user("systemctl --user show " + worker + " -p InvocationID --value").strip()
        user("systemctl --user restart workspace-portal@fixture")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command), timeout=60)
        current = operation(slug)
        assert current["receiptId"] == accepted["receiptId"] and current["attempt"] == accepted["attempt"], current
        assert before == user("systemctl --user show " + worker + " -p InvocationID --value").strip()
        user("systemctl --user stop " + holder)
        archived(slug, checkout)
        revive(slug, checkout)

    with subtest("portal restart and worker interruption preserve admitted identity"):
        slug = "2026-10-17-restart"
        checkout = fixture(slug)
        # Test-only systemd pre-exec barrier; the archive executable is unchanged.
        dropin = "/home/developer/.config/systemd/user/workspace-archive-.service.d"
        user("mkdir -p " + dropin)
        user("printf '[Service]\\nExecStartPre=/nix/store/gph17gb73p6qbrqqjnypfjj5npf0ldyx-coreutils-9.11/bin/sleep infinity\\n' > " + dropin + "/barrier.conf")
        user("systemctl --user daemon-reload")
        accepted = browser(slug, "archive")
        worker = unit(accepted)
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "systemctl --user show " + worker + " -p SubState --value | grep start-pre")
        user("systemctl --user restart workspace-portal@fixture")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "test -S /run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/portal.sock")
        # Restored receipts start paused until the background reconciler
        # proves the still-running supervised worker. Socket readiness
        # alone does not prove that reconciliation has finished.
        command = "curl -fsS --unix-socket /run/user/1000/dev-workspaces/fixture/portal.sock "
        command += "http://localhost/api/sessions/" + slug + "/operation"
        command += " | /nix/store/xqnbm0vgqcq9b1b54c80qj9s0qhbwa08-python3-3.13.15/bin/python3 -c " + shlex.quote(
            "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); "
            "assert d.get('receiptId') == " + repr(accepted["receiptId"]) +
            " and d.get('state') == 'running', d; print(json.dumps(d))")
        machine.wait_until_succeeds(user_prefix + "sh -c " + shlex.quote(command), timeout=60)
        user("systemctl --user kill --signal=SIGKILL --kill-whom=all " + worker)
        wait_operation(slug, "failed")
        user("rm " + dropin + "/barrier.conf && systemctl --user daemon-reload")
        retried = browser(slug, "retry")
        assert retried["receiptId"] == accepted["receiptId"]
        assert retried["options"]["journalId"] == accepted["options"]["journalId"]
        assert retried["attempt"] == accepted["attempt"] + 1
        archived(slug, checkout)
        revive(slug, checkout)

    with subtest("retry after checkout removal keeps the recovery snapshot"):
        slug = "2026-10-17-recovery"
        checkout = fixture(slug)
        user("chmod 0500 " + root + "/archive")
        accepted = browser(slug, "archive")
        wait_operation(slug, "failed")
        user("test ! -e " + checkout)
        journal = root + "/worktrees/.locks/" + slug + ".archive.json"
        retained = json.loads(user("cat " + journal))
        assert retained["operation_id"] == accepted["options"]["journalId"]
        recovery = state + "/archived-worktrees/"
        before = user("find " + recovery + " -type f -exec sha256sum {} \\; | sort")
        user("chmod 0755 " + root + "/archive")
        browser(slug, "retry")
        archived(slug, checkout)
        assert user("find " + recovery + " -type f -exec sha256sum {} \\; | sort") == before
        revive(slug, checkout)

    with subtest("tracking Git failure does not fail local archival"):
        slug = "2026-10-17-offline"
        checkout = fixture(slug)
        user("mv ~/origins/workspace.git ~/origins/workspace.offline")
        browser(slug, "archive")
        archived(slug, checkout)
        user("cd " + root + " && " + cli + " tracking-sync --slug " + slug + " --force --json")
        result = json.loads(user("cd " + root + " && " + cli + " tracking-sync --status --slug " + slug + " --json"))
        assert result[0]["state"] == "pending" and result[0]["error"], result
        user("mv ~/origins/workspace.offline ~/origins/workspace.git")
        user("cd " + root + " && " + cli + " tracking-sync --slug " + slug + " --force --json")
        result = json.loads(user("cd " + root + " && " + cli + " tracking-sync --status --slug " + slug + " --json"))
        assert result[0]["state"] == "synced", result
        revive(slug, checkout)
except Exception:
    diagnostics()
    raise

structuredAttrs.name: gcc-16.2.0
structuredAttrs.postConfigure:
# Avoid store paths when embedding ./configure flags into gcc.
# Mangled arguments are still useful when reporting bugs upstream.
sed -e "/TOPLEVEL_CONFIGURE_ARGUMENTS=/ s|$NIX_STORE/[a-z0-9]\{32\}-|$NIX_STORE/eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee-|g" -i Makefile
structuredAttrs.postInstall:
# Clean up our compatibility symlinks (see above)
for link in "${compatibilitySymlinks[@]}"; do
  echo "Removing compatibility symlink: $link"
  rm -f "$link"
done

# Move target runtime libraries to lib output.
# For non-cross, they're in $out/lib; for cross, they're in $out/$targetConfig/lib.
targetLibDir="${targetConfig+$targetConfig/}lib"

moveToOutput "$targetLibDir/lib*.so*" "${!outputLib}"
moveToOutput "$targetLibDir/lib*.dylib" "${!outputLib}"
moveToOutput "$targetLibDir/lib*.dll.a" "${!outputLib}"
moveToOutput "$targetLibDir/lib*.dll" "${!outputLib}"
moveToOutput "share/gcc-*/python" "${!outputLib}"

if [ -z "$enableShared" ]; then
    moveToOutput "$targetLibDir/lib*.a" "${!outputLib}"
fi

for i in "${!outputLib}"/$targetLibDir/*.py; do
    substituteInPlace "$i" --replace "$out" "${!outputLib}"
done

# Multilib and cross can't exist at the same time, so just use lib64 here
if [ -n "$enableMultilib" ]; then
    moveToOutput "lib64/lib*.so*" "${!outputLib}"
    moveToOutput "lib64/lib*.dylib" "${!outputLib}"
    moveToOutput "lib64/lib*.dll.a" "${!outputLib}"
    moveToOutput "lib64/lib*.dll" "${!outputLib}"

    for i in "${!outputLib}"/lib64/*.py; do
        substituteInPlace "$i" --replace "$out" "${!outputLib}"
    done
fi

# Remove `fixincl' to prevent a retained dependency on the
# previous gcc.
rm -rf $out/libexec/gcc/*/*/install-tools
rm -rf $out/lib/gcc/*/*/install-tools

# More dependencies with the previous gcc or some libs (gccbug stores the build command line)
rm -rf $out/bin/gccbug

# Remove .la files, they're not adjusted for the makeCompatibilitySymlink magic,
# which confuses libtool and leads to weird linking errors.
# Removing the files just makes libtool link .so files directly, which is usually
# what we want anyway.
find $out -name '*.la' -delete

if type "install_name_tool"; then
    for i in "${!outputLib}"/lib/*.*.dylib "${!outputLib}"/lib/*.so.[0-9]; do
        install_name_tool -id "$i" "$i" || true
        for old_path in $(otool -L "$i" | grep "$out" | awk '{print $1}'); do
          new_path=`echo "$old_path" | sed "s,$out,${!outputLib},"`
          install_name_tool -change "$old_path" "$new_path" "$i" || true
        done
    done
fi

structuredAttrs.preUnpack:
oldOpts="$(shopt -po nounset)" || true
set -euo pipefail

export NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY="$NIX_BUILD_TOP/dummy"
mkdir "$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY"

if test "$staticCompiler" = "1"; then
    EXTRA_LDFLAGS="-static"
elif test "${NIX_DONT_SET_RPATH-}" != "1"; then
    EXTRA_LDFLAGS="-Wl,-rpath,${!outputLib}/lib"
else
    EXTRA_LDFLAGS=""
fi

# GCC interprets empty paths as ".", which we don't want.
if test -z "${CPATH-}"; then unset CPATH; fi
if test -z "${LIBRARY_PATH-}"; then unset LIBRARY_PATH; fi
echo "\$CPATH is \`${CPATH-}'"
echo "\$LIBRARY_PATH is \`${LIBRARY_PATH-}'"

if test "$noSysDirs" = "1"; then

    declare -g \
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD EXTRA_FLAGS EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET \
        EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET

    # Extract flags from Bintools Wrappers
    for post in '_FOR_BUILD' ""; do
        curBintools="NIX_BINTOOLS${post}"

        declare -a extraLDFlags=()
        if [[ -e "${!curBintools}/nix-support/orig-libc" ]]; then
            # Figure out what extra flags when linking to pass to the gcc
            # compilers being generated to make sure that they use our libc.
            extraLDFlags=($(< "${!curBintools}/nix-support/libc-ldflags") $(< "${!curBintools}/nix-support/libc-ldflags-before" || true))
            if [ -e ${!curBintools}/nix-support/ld-set-dynamic-linker ]; then
                extraLDFlags=-dynamic-linker=$(< ${!curBintools}/nix-support/dynamic-linker)
            fi

            # The path to the Libc binaries such as `crti.o'.
            libc_libdir="$(< "${!curBintools}/nix-support/orig-libc")/lib"
        else
            # Hack: support impure environments.
            extraLDFlags=("-L/usr/lib64" "-L/usr/lib")
            libc_libdir="/usr/lib"
        fi
        declare -a prefixExtraLDFlags=()
        prefixExtraLDFlags=("-L$libc_libdir")
        nixDontSetRpathVar=NIX_DONT_SET_RPATH${post}
        if test "${!nixDontSetRpathVar-}" != "1"; then
            prefixExtraLDFlags+=("-rpath" "$libc_libdir")
        fi
        extraLDFlags=("${prefixExtraLDFlags[@]}" "${extraLDFlags[@]}")
        for i in "${extraLDFlags[@]}"; do
            declare -g EXTRA_LDFLAGS${post}+=" -Wl,$i"
        done
    done

    # Extract flags from CC Wrappers
    for post in '_FOR_BUILD' ""; do
        curCC="NIX_CC${post}"
        curFIXINC="NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY${post}"

        declare -a extraFlags=()
        if [[ -e "${!curCC}/nix-support/orig-libc" ]]; then
            # Figure out what extra compiling flags to pass to the gcc compilers
            # being generated to make sure that they use our libc.
            extraFlags=($(< "${!curCC}/nix-support/libc-crt1-cflags") $(< "${!curCC}/nix-support/libc-cflags"))

            # The path to the Libc headers
            libc_devdir="$(< "${!curCC}/nix-support/orig-libc-dev")"

            # Use *real* header files, otherwise a limits.h is generated that
            # does not include Libc's limits.h (notably missing SSIZE_MAX,
            # which breaks the build).
            declare -g NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY${post}="$libc_devdir/include"
        else
            # Hack: support impure environments.
            extraFlags=("-isystem" "/usr/include")
            declare -g NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY${post}=/usr/include
        fi

        extraFlags=("-I${!curFIXINC}" "${extraFlags[@]}")

        # BOOT_CFLAGS defaults to `-g -O2'; since we override it below, make
        # sure to explictly add them so that files compiled with the bootstrap
        # compiler are optimized and (optionally) contain debugging information
        # (info "(gccinstall) Building").
        if test -n "${dontStrip-}"; then
            extraFlags=("-O2" "-g" "${extraFlags[@]}")
        else
            # Don't pass `-g' at all; this saves space while building.
            extraFlags=("-O2" "${extraFlags[@]}")
        fi

        declare -g EXTRA_FLAGS${post}="${extraFlags[*]}"
    done

    if test -z "${targetConfig-}"; then
        # host = target, so the flags are the same
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET="$EXTRA_FLAGS"
        EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET="$EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
    fi

    # We include `-fmacro-prefix-map` in `cc-wrapper` for non‐GCC
    # platforms only, but they get picked up and passed down to
    # e.g. GFortran calls that complain about the option not
    # applying to the language. Hack around it by asking GCC not
    # to complain.
    #
    # TODO: Someone please fix this to do things that make sense.
    if [[ $EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD == *-fmacro-prefix-map* ]]; then
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD+=" -Wno-complain-wrong-lang"
    fi
    if [[ $EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET == *-fmacro-prefix-map* ]]; then
        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET+=" -Wno-complain-wrong-lang"
    fi

    # CFLAGS_FOR_TARGET are needed for the libstdc++ configure script to find
    # the startfiles.
    # FLAGS_FOR_TARGET are needed for the target libraries to receive the -Bxxx
    # for the startfiles.
    makeFlagsArray+=(
        "BUILD_SYSTEM_HEADER_DIR=$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY_FOR_BUILD"
        "SYSTEM_HEADER_DIR=$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY_FOR_BUILD"
        "NATIVE_SYSTEM_HEADER_DIR=$NIX_FIXINC_DUMMY"

        "LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"
        #"LDFLAGS=$EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
        "LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"

        "CFLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"
        "CXXFLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"
        "FLAGS_FOR_BUILD=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_BUILD $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_BUILD"

        # It seems there is a bug in GCC 5
        #"CFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS $EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
        #"CXXFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS $EXTRA_LDFLAGS"

        "CFLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
        "CXXFLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
        "FLAGS_FOR_TARGET=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
    )

    if test -z "${targetConfig-}"; then
        makeFlagsArray+=(
            "BOOT_CFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS $EXTRA_LDFLAGS"
            "BOOT_LDFLAGS=$EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET $EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET"
        )
    fi

    if test "$withoutTargetLibc" == 1; then
        # We don't want the gcc build to assume there will be a libc providing
        # limits.h in this stage
        makeFlagsArray+=(
            'LIMITS_H_TEST=false'
        )
    else
        makeFlagsArray+=(
            'LIMITS_H_TEST=true'
        )
    fi
fi

structuredAttrs.postFetch:
tmpfile="$TMPDIR/patch"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Fetched patch file '$out' is empty!" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

set +e
cat < "$out" > "$tmpfile"
if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
    echo 'Failed to decode patch with command "'cat'"' >&2
    echo 'Fetched file was (limited to 128 bytes):' >&2
    od -A x -t x1z -v -N 128 "$out" >&2
    exit 1
fi
set -e
mv "$tmpfile" "$out"

lsdiff \
   \
  "$out" \
| sort -u | sed -e 's/[*?]/\\&/g' \
| xargs -I{} --delimiter='\n' \
  filterdiff \
  --include={} \
  --strip=0 \
   \
  --clean "$out" > "$tmpfile"

if [ ! -s "$tmpfile" ]; then
  echo "error: Normalized patch '$tmpfile' is empty (while the fetched file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Did you maybe fetch a HTML representation of a patch instead of a raw patch?" 1>&2
  echo "Fetched file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$out" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

filterdiff \
  -p1 \
   \
   \
   \
  "$tmpfile" > "$out"

if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
  echo "error: Filtered patch '$out' is empty (while the original patch file was not)!" 1>&2
  echo "Check your includes and excludes." 1>&2
  echo "Normalized patch file was:" 1>&2
  cat "$tmpfile" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

env.preConfigure:
# build uses `git describe` to set the build version
cat > $NIX_BUILD_TOP/git << "EOF"
#!/nix/store/rzl7zd3zx56vl7m55x1l49sr4xx2bb7y-bash-5.3p9/bin/bash
echo v3.12.1
EOF
chmod +x $NIX_BUILD_TOP/git
export PATH=$NIX_BUILD_TOP:$PATH

env.buildPhase:
runHook preBuild

exclude='\(/_\|examples\|Godeps\|testdata'
if [[ -n "$excludedPackages" ]]; then
  IFS=' ' read -r -a excludedArr <<<"${excludedPackages[@]}"
  printf -v excludedAlternates '%s\\|' "${excludedArr[@]}"
  excludedAlternates=${excludedAlternates%\\|} # drop final \| added by printf
  exclude+='\|'"$excludedAlternates"
fi
exclude+='\)'

buildGoDir() {
  local cmd="$1" dir="$2"

  declare -a flags
  flags+=(${tags:+-tags=$(concatStringsSep "," tags)})
  flags+=(${ldflags:+-ldflags="${ldflags[*]}"})
  flags+=("-p" "$NIX_BUILD_CORES")
  if (( "${NIX_DEBUG:-0}" >= 1 )); then
    flags+=(-x)
  fi

  if [ "$cmd" = "test" ]; then
    flags+=(-vet=off)
    flags+=($checkFlags)
  fi

  local OUT
  if ! OUT="$(go $cmd "${flags[@]}" $dir 2>&1)"; then
    if ! echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '(no( buildable| non-test)?|build constraints exclude all) Go (source )?files'; then
      echo "$OUT" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT" >&2
  fi
  return 0
}

getGoDirs() {
  local type;
  type="$1"
  if [ -n "$subPackages" ]; then
    echo "$subPackages" | sed "s,\(^\| \),\1./,g"
  else
    find . -type f -name \*$type.go -exec dirname {} \; | grep -v "/vendor/" | sort --unique | grep -v "$exclude"
  fi
}

if [ -z "$enableParallelBuilding" ]; then
    export NIX_BUILD_CORES=1
fi
for pkg in $(getGoDirs ""); do
  echo "Building subPackage $pkg"
buildGoDir install "$pkg"

done
runHook postBuild

  echo "int main() { return 77; }" > "$f"

sed '2i echo "Skipping test: ls/removed-directory" && exit 77' -i ./tests/ls/removed-directory.sh

sed '2i echo Skipping du inacc-dir test && exit 77' -i ./tests/du/inacc-dir.sh
